technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring-based module and build conventions rather than introducing a new application framework.

For message-bus and binding selection, inspect dependency metadata and available binding implementations, then apply an explicit deterministic selection order with a documented fallback when no binding is configured.
Use Maven-compatible dependency resolution for runtime module dependencies, with conflict mediation based on direct-dependency precedence and nearest or explicitly managed versions.
Isolate incompatible runtime module dependencies with classloader boundaries where practical; otherwise fail deployment with a clear diagnostic rather than silently loading an incompatible version.
Implement single-node undeploy through a deployment registry that tracks running stream components and performs graceful stop, cleanup, and idempotent repeated undeploy requests.
Use Spring profiles to select repository implementations through conditional bean configuration, including a local profile backed by an in-memory metadata repository.
Expose counter metrics through Spring-compatible HTTP endpoints using a small, stable endpoint contract suitable for dashboard polling.
Package the application as a Docker image and publish it through an automated DockerHub workflow triggered by approved commits or tags.
Create the public screencast from a reproducible firehose/counter demonstration with documented startup and execution steps.
Produce an architecture/design document for porting XD modules to s-c-s modules, covering module contracts, lifecycle, configuration, dependency handling, and migration sequencing.
assumptions: The existing repository, build, test, and deployment infrastructure is available and can be modified; no greenfield project setup is required.
The increment is implemented by one developer, and estimates represent active work-hours only, excluding elapsed waiting time, meetings unrelated to the increment, and external approval delays.
The current codebase already supports Java 17 and a compatible Spring version, or only minor build changes are needed to maintain compatibility.
The dependency-resolution implementation is limited to the runtime needs of the existing module and does not attempt to replace Maven or Gradle as a general-purpose build system.
The local profile only requires an in-memory repository and one existing or representative persistent repository strategy is sufficient to validate profile selection.
Single-node undeploy targets streams and uses the existing job and stream lifecycle abstractions; distributed undeploy and production-grade orchestration are out of scope.
Counter metrics are read-only HTTP endpoints and do not require a full metrics aggregation, alerting, or dashboard product.
DockerHub credentials, repository ownership, and CI access are available; security review and organizational release approval are not included.
The screencast can use an existing or minimally modified firehose/counter sample and requires basic editing, captions, and publication rather than professional video production.
The design work for porting XD modules produces an actionable technical proposal and prototype-level examples, not a complete module migration.
Normal unit, integration, documentation, and regression testing are included, but exhaustive compatibility testing across all application servers and JVM versions is not.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build files, lifecycle APIs, repository abstractions, deployment samples, test conventions, and CI configuration; identify integration points and establish the implementation plan.
Investigate how message-bus and binding jars are currently discovered, included, excluded, and loaded; compare feasible selection and fallback mechanisms and record the recommended design.

Implement configuration and runtime logic for selecting binding implementations, excluding conflicting or unwanted jars where supported, and applying the documented fallback when no binding is configured.
Add unit and integration tests for configured bindings, absent bindings, multiple candidates, and invalid selections; document configuration, precedence, and fallback behavior.

Define dependency coordinates, repository lookup, version conflict mediation, transitive dependency handling, classloader boundaries, error reporting, caching, and security limitations for runtime resolution.

Integrate a Maven-compatible resolver, implement dependency graph resolution and conflict handling, download or locate required artifacts, construct runtime classpaths or classloaders, and expose diagnostics for failures.
Test direct and transitive dependencies, conflicting versions, managed versions, missing artifacts, cached artifacts, multiple modules, and representative Spring Data or binding-version scenarios.
Create or update the Dockerfile and supporting packaging scripts, define runtime configuration and image metadata, and verify that the application starts correctly from the produced image.
Configure CI credentials and image tagging, implement DockerHub push automation for approved commits or tags, and validate a complete build, push, pull, and run cycle.
Document image naming, tags, required credentials, publication commands, rollback expectations, and local verification steps.
Prepare the public firehose/counter demonstration, verify prerequisites, create a concise script, and ensure the sample exercises the intended developer workflow.
Record the demonstration, perform basic editing and captions, publish it publicly, and add reproducibility links and instructions.

Review the existing deployment lifecycle and referenced undeploy proposal, define state transitions, graceful shutdown, resource cleanup, idempotency, error handling, and consistency requirements for jobs and streams.

Implement the undeploy command/API for the single-JVM target, connect it to the deployment registry and running components, perform graceful termination and cleanup, and return useful operation status.
Add tests for successful undeploy, unknown deployments, repeated requests, failed shutdown, cleanup, concurrent operations, and representative stream and job lifecycle cases.
Map profile activation to repository implementations, define default-profile behavior, configuration properties, bean conditionality, and compatibility with existing Admin startup paths.
Add Spring profile configuration and conditional repository beans, implement or connect the local in-memory metadata repository, and update startup and configuration handling.
Test profile activation, default behavior, in-memory persistence semantics, repository selection, configuration errors, and application startup under each supported profile.

Analyze existing XD modules and s-c-s conventions; define module boundaries, contracts, configuration model, lifecycle, packaging, dependency rules, compatibility strategy, and a prioritized migration plan.
Create representative module and configuration examples, review the proposed foundation against existing use cases, resolve design issues, and publish the actionable design document.
Define counter names, dimensions, lifecycle and reset semantics, endpoint paths, response format, access behavior, and compatibility with the firehose/counter demonstration.
Instrument the counter processing path, add HTTP endpoints and serialization, connect endpoint data to the running stream state, and provide configuration for endpoint exposure.
Test counter increments, multiple streams, empty and unavailable states, endpoint responses, serialization, concurrent reads, and integration with the demonstration pipeline.

Run the complete build and regression suite, exercise dependency resolution, profiles, undeploy, Docker startup, and counter endpoints together, fix integration defects, and update final documentation.
